result:
Solution 1 is the only one whose count I could confirm. I checked it by deriving the structure of the achievable sets and recounting.

**Structure of the achievable sets.** Write the plane as ax + by + cz = d. Take the bottom base at height 0 and the top base at height h, and let f(k) = a·x_k + b·y_k be the same linear function on both decagons. The bottom vertices in M are those with f > d, and the top vertices in M are those with f > d − ch. These two thresholds can be chosen independently. So M is a pair (A, B) of "upper level sets" of the same f on the two decagons. For a generic direction of (a, b), these level sets are the initial segments of a single ordering of the 10 vertices. There are 20 such orderings (chains), and each chain has sets of every size from 0 to 10.

**Counting the pairs.**
- Pairs where A or B is empty or full: there are 92 arcs on each base (empty, full, and 90 proper arcs). So there are 92² − 90² = 364 such pairs. Removing the all-empty and all-full sets, which are not genuine two-part partitions, leaves 362. This matches Solution 1.
- Pairs where both arcs are proper (sizes 1 to 9): each chain contributes 9² = 81 pairs, so the 20 chains give 1620. A pair is counted twice exactly when both arcs have the same center, meaning the same vertex for odd sizes or the same gap for even sizes. Even-even pairs number 10·16 = 160 and odd-odd pairs number 10·25 = 250, so 410 pairs are double counted. The distinct count is 1620 − 410 = 1210.

The total is 362 + 1210 = 1572.

**The other two solutions.** Solution 2 gives 1894 with no real derivation. Solution 3 requires a shared "ending vertex" and gets 1172. That condition is wrong, because nested arcs with a common center can also be achieved, as in the even-even and odd-odd cases above.

CHOICE: 1
